what: Estimated prover cells per call and per byte for the execution-only candidate curve, field and Keccak-sponge services (tags 0x0003_01xx), same shape as calibration.json candidate_services. Excludes the ECALL and the guest's packet set-up, which the CPU coefficient already charges. Derivations: candidate-curve-costs.md; ABI: notes/candidate-curves-abi.md.

bn254_g1_add.derivation: Affine chord rule as ZisK Bn254CurveAdd: 3 product relations (lambda*(x2-x1) = y2-y1, x3 = lambda^2-x1-x2, y3 = lambda*(x1-x3)-y1, each a*b+linear = q*p) x 703 = 2109; x1 != x2 by a chunk inverse 100; bridge 6 coordinates (p, q read; r written) x 378 = 2268; RAM 16 reads + 8 writes = 2304; 3 pointer packet words x 190 = 570; canonical checks 6 x 70 = 420. Raw 7771 x 1.3 -> 10100.

bn254_g1_double.derivation: Affine tangent rule as ZisK Bn254CurveDbl: lambda*2y = 3x^2 (two products, 1.5 rows), x3 = lambda^2-2x, y3 = lambda*(x-x3)-y: 3.5 x 703 = 2461; y != 0 chunk inverse 100; bridge 4 coordinates x 378 = 1512; RAM 8 + 8 = 1536; 2 pointer words = 380; canonical 4 x 70 = 280. Raw 6269 x 1.3 -> 8200.

bn254_fp2_mul.derivation: As ZisK Bn254ComplexMul: c0 = a0 b0 - a1 b1 + q0 p and c1 = a0 b1 + a1 b0 - q1 p, each a two-product relation (1.5 rows): 3 x 703 = 2109; outputs canonical 2 x 70 = 140 (inputs need not be); bridge 6 coordinates = 2268; RAM 16 + 8 = 2304; 3 pointer words = 570. Raw 7391 x 1.3 -> 9600.

bls12_381_g1_add.derivation: bn254_g1_add at 384 bits in the Montgomery domain (a*b = r*2^384 + q*p, same row shape): 3 x 1055 = 3165; x-difference 150; bridge 6 x 567 = 3402; RAM 24 + 12 = 3456; packet 570; canonical 6 x 105 = 630. Raw 11373 x 1.3 -> 14800. Not used by the client in this round.

bls12_381_g1_double.derivation: bn254_g1_double at 384 bits: 3.5 x 1055 = 3693; y != 0 150; bridge 4 x 567 = 2268; RAM 12 + 12 = 2304; packet 380; canonical 4 x 105 = 420. Raw 9215 x 1.3 -> 12000. Not used by the client in this round.

bls12_381_fp2_mul.derivation: As ZisK Bls12_381ComplexMul in Montgomery form (blst's representation): two two-product relations, 3 x 1055 = 3165; bridge 6 x 567 = 3402; RAM 24 + 12 = 3456; packet 570; output canonical 2 x 105 = 210. Raw 10803 x 1.3 -> 14000.

arith384_mod.derivation: As ZisK Arith384Mod: arith256_mod's truth (1100: 512-bit quotient, r < m, m = 0 flag) x 1.5 = 1650; bridge 5 x 567 = 2835; RAM 30 x 96 = 2880; 5 pointer words = 950. Raw 8315 x 1.3 -> 10800. Not used by the client in this round.

arith384_mont.derivation: a*b = r*2^384 + q*m (Montgomery product; same row as a*b = q*m + r): one 384-bit product row 1055; m odd (low limb bit) 10; r < m 105; bridge a, b, m read, r written = 4 x 567 = 2268; RAM 18 + 6 = 2304; 4 pointer words = 760. Raw 6502 x 1.3 -> 8500. A fixed-modulus variant saves the m read (~1500 cells).

keccak_sponge.derivation: bytes = 136 x permutations (rate bytes absorbed, including the padded final block). Per permutation: Keccak truth 65525 (measured, layout.zig) plus absorb: 17 input words via RAM 1632, byte realignment 17 x 60 = 1020, 1088 input bit columns XORed into the rate 1100, state chaining between consecutive permutations 500 -> 4252 x 1.3 = 5528; 71053 / 136 = 523 per byte. Per call: final state 25 words through the Keccak bridge (25 x 182 = 4550) and RAM (2400), 4 packet words 760, padding one-hot row 300, length/descriptor 200 -> 8210 x 1.3 -> 10700 (fresh-state calls; a non-fresh call also reads 25 lanes, about +9000, not used by the client).
